knowledge_documents.title: Root Canal Treatment — What to Expect
knowledge_documents.content:
Root Canal Treatment — What to Expect

Most root canal treatments at Smile Care Dental Clinic take 1 to 2 visits, depending on the tooth and severity of infection. A straightforward case can often be completed in a single visit; more complex cases (e.g. molars with multiple canals, or significant infection) may need a follow-up visit about a week later.

Pain expectations, honestly: local anesthesia is used throughout the procedure, so you should not feel sharp pain during the treatment itself — most patients feel pressure or vibration, not pain. It is normal to have mild soreness or tenderness in the treated tooth and surrounding gum for 2-3 days afterward, especially when biting down. This is manageable with over-the-counter pain relief (e.g. paracetamol/ibuprofen as advised) and is not a sign anything went wrong.

Recovery: most patients return to normal eating and daily activities the next day, avoiding chewing on the treated side until any soreness settles and, if a crown is planned, until that's placed. A temporary filling or crown is usually placed first; a permanent crown is typically recommended afterward to protect the tooth long-term.

Aftercare: avoid chewing hard or sticky foods on the treated tooth for the first few days, keep up gentle brushing and flossing, and take any prescribed antibiotics or pain medication as directed. Contact the clinic if you experience severe pain, swelling, or a fever after the procedure — mild discomfort is normal, but these are not.

knowledge_documents.title: Tooth Extraction — What to Expect
knowledge_documents.content:
Tooth Extraction — What to Expect

The area is fully numbed with local anesthesia before the tooth is removed, so you should not feel pain during the extraction itself — you may feel pressure or pulling sensations. After the anesthesia wears off (usually a few hours later), some soreness, mild swelling, and minor bleeding are completely normal for the first 24 hours.

What's normal: light oozing of blood for a few hours (biting gently on the gauze provided controls this), swelling that peaks around day 2 and then improves, and mild-to-moderate discomfort manageable with the pain relief the dentist recommends or prescribes.

Aftercare instructions: apply an ice pack to the outside of the cheek for the first 24 hours to reduce swelling, stick to soft, cool foods (yogurt, soup, mashed potato) for the first day or two, avoid rinsing, spitting forcefully, or using a straw for 24 hours (this can dislodge the healing blood clot), and avoid smoking for at least 48 hours, as it significantly slows healing and increases the risk of complications.

When to call the clinic instead of waiting: heavy bleeding that doesn't slow down after firm gauze pressure for 30 minutes, severe pain that worsens after day 2-3 rather than improving, a fever, or a bad taste/odor from the socket (possible signs of infection or "dry socket"). These are real reasons to call the front desk directly, not something to wait out.

knowledge_documents.title: Parking & Location
knowledge_documents.content: Smile Care Dental Clinic has free on-site parking available for patients right outside the building — no need to search for street parking. The clinic is located in New Baneshwor, Kathmandu, near the Bhrikutimandap intersection, a well-known landmark. If you're arriving by taxi or ride-share, just tell the driver "New Baneshwor, near Bhrikutimandap, Smile Care Dental Clinic" and they will know the area. The clinic is also a short walk from the New Baneshwor bus stop for patients using public transport. Look for the clinic's signboard on the main road — the entrance and parking area are on the ground floor.

knowledge_documents.title: Teeth Cleaning — What to Expect
knowledge_documents.content:
Teeth Cleaning (Scaling & Polishing) — What to Expect

A professional cleaning is not painful for most patients. You may feel some mild pressure or vibration from the scaling tool as plaque and tartar are removed, and if your gums are inflamed or you have sensitive teeth, you might notice brief, mild sensitivity to cold water during or shortly after the cleaning — this is temporary and settles within a day.

The process: scaling removes plaque and tartar buildup from the tooth surface and along the gumline, and polishing smooths and cleans the tooth surface afterward, leaving teeth feeling noticeably smoother. The whole appointment typically takes about 30 minutes.

How often it's recommended: for most patients, a professional cleaning every 6 months is recommended to keep gums healthy and catch any issues early. Patients with a history of gum disease or heavier tartar buildup may be advised to come in more often, e.g. every 3-4 months.

knowledge_documents.title: Payment & Cancellation Policy
knowledge_documents.content:
Payment & Cancellation Policy

Payment methods: Smile Care Dental Clinic accepts both cash and card payments. Payment is collected at the clinic after your appointment, unless otherwise arranged in advance.

Cancellation policy: we kindly ask for at least 24 hours' notice if you need to cancel or reschedule an appointment. This lets us offer the slot to another patient who may need it. Please call the front desk or message us as soon as you know you need to change your appointment.

Advance/deposit policy for higher-cost procedures: for larger treatments such as Root Canal Treatment, Full Braces Treatment, and Dental Implants, we request a 20% advance deposit at the time of booking to confirm the appointment slot, with the remaining balance due at the time of treatment. This deposit is credited toward your total treatment cost — it is not an additional charge. For routine appointments (consultations, cleanings, fillings, extractions), no advance deposit is required.

knowledge_documents.title: Braces — Process & Timeline
knowledge_documents.content:
Braces — Process & Timeline

The typical journey: (1) a Braces Consultation appointment, where Dr. Sunita Koirala assesses your teeth and bite, discusses goals, and puts together a treatment plan; (2) the Full Braces Treatment fitting appointment, where the braces are actually placed — this initial fitting takes about an hour; (3) regular adjustment visits, usually every 4-6 weeks, where wires/bands are tightened or adjusted to keep teeth moving correctly.

Duration: most full orthodontic treatments take between 1 and 2.5 years, depending on the complexity of the case, patient age, and how consistently any take-home instructions (like rubber bands) are followed. Dr. Koirala will give you a more specific estimate at your consultation once she's assessed your teeth.

Does it hurt: getting braces fitted itself is not painful, though your mouth may feel a little unusual for the first day or two as you adjust to the brackets and wires. After each adjustment visit, it's normal to feel pressure or soreness in your teeth for 2-4 days — this is a sign the braces are working, not something to worry about. Over-the-counter pain relief and sticking to softer foods for those first couple of days after each adjustment usually helps.

Cost expectations: the Braces Consultation is NPR 800 and is a separate, standalone appointment. Full Braces Treatment is priced at NPR 60,000, which covers the initial fitting; ongoing adjustment visits are part of the overall treatment plan discussed at your consultation — ask the front desk or Dr. Koirala for the specific payment schedule for your case, as this can vary depending on your treatment plan.

knowledge_documents.title: Emergency Dental Care
knowledge_documents.content:
Emergency Dental Care

What counts as a real dental emergency: severe, unrelenting tooth or jaw pain that isn't relieved by over-the-counter pain medication; significant facial or gum swelling, especially if it's spreading or affecting your ability to swallow or breathe; a knocked-out or badly broken tooth from an injury or trauma; uncontrolled bleeding from the mouth that doesn't stop with firm gauze pressure; and a fever accompanying dental pain or swelling (a possible sign of a spreading infection).

What to do: if you're experiencing any of the above, please call our front desk directly right away rather than waiting for a chat response — a real emergency needs a real person on the phone who can advise you immediately and fit you in urgently. Our phone number is +977-1-4781234. If it's outside clinic hours and the situation feels severe (heavy uncontrolled bleeding, difficulty breathing/swallowing, facial trauma), please go to your nearest hospital emergency department rather than waiting until we reopen.

For non-emergency concerns — like mild sensitivity, a small chip, or general questions — a regular appointment booked through chat or a phone call is the right path, and there's no need to treat it as urgent.
